title: The adjoint kernel has a unipotent quotient with central kernel
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and their homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], and closed subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type; smoothness, connectedness and finite type are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $\mathfrak g=T_eG$ for the tangent space at the identity and $\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$ for the group scheme of invertible linear maps of this finite-dimensional vector space. Let $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$ be the representation obtained by differentiating conjugation, and let $N=\ker\operatorname{Ad}$. Let $Z(G)$ be the closed subgroup scheme whose $A$-points commute with every element of $G(A')$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$, as in [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. For $n\geq1$, let $\mathcal U_{n,F}$ be the group scheme with $\mathcal U_{n,F}(A)$ the upper triangular $n\times n$ matrices over $A$ with every diagonal entry $1$, under matrix multiplication. There exist $n\geq1$, a closed subgroup scheme $U\subseteq\mathcal U_{n,F}$, and a group-scheme homomorphism $q:N\to U$ whose scheme-theoretic kernel is $Z(G)\subseteq N$. In particular, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $g\in N(A)$, one has $q_A(g)=1$ if and only if $g\in Z(G)(A)$. No reductivity of $G$, and no smoothness or connectedness of $N$ or $U$, is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 14.23, printed p.285; Theorem 14.5(a),(b), printed p.281; quotient with its scheme-theoretic kernel and affineness in Theorem 5.28 and Proposition 5.29, printed p.105. The assertion records the quotient N/Z(G) through a closed unitriangular embedding, without needing quotient terminology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-conjugation-finite-jet-kernel] to $G$ and choose $r\geq\max(1,r_0)$. Write $V=B/I^{r+1}$ and $J^i=I^i/I^{r+1}$. The representation $\rho_r$ preserves these subspaces and has scheme-theoretic kernel $Z(G)$. A central element induces identity conjugation after every base change; differentiating gives $\operatorname{Ad}=1$. Thus $Z(G)\subseteq N$, and the restriction $h=\rho_r|_N$ has kernel exactly $Z(G)$, on every test algebra.

source.place: Proposition 14.23, first and third sentences of proof; Corollary 8.10, printed pp.150,285.

proof.text: The cotangent action of $N$ is trivial, including over nonreduced test algebras. At $e$, [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] identifies $\mathfrak g$ with $(I/I^2)^\vee$ and differentiation with dual pullback. Here is the formula after an arbitrary extension to an $F$-algebra $A$: a tangent vector is the map $f\mapsto e^*(f)+\epsilon\lambda([f-e^*(f)])$ to $A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, with $\lambda:A\otimes_F(I/I^2)\to A$ linear. Under conjugation by $g^{-1}$ it becomes the same expression with $\lambda$ composed with pullback on $A\otimes_F(I/I^2)$. This follows just by substituting the pulled-back function into the displayed formula. For $g\in N(A)$ its tangent action $\operatorname{Ad}(g^{-1})$ is identity. Every $\lambda$ is therefore unchanged. Applying the dual basis of the finite free module $A\otimes_F(I/I^2)$ shows its pullback is identity. Thus $g$ acts trivially on the first ideal quotient. This is the contragredient convention used in Milne 14.23.

source.place: Proposition 14.23, second sentence of proof; paragraphs 10.19--10.20, printed pp.192,285.

proof.text: For every $i\geq1$, $I^i/I^{i+1}$ is spanned over $F$ by products of $i$ elements of $I/I^2$. Indeed, elements of $I^i$ are sums of products $b x_1\cdots x_i$ with $x_j\in I$, and $b$ can be replaced by its residue $e^*(b)$ modulo $I^{i+1}$. For any test algebra $A$, each $g\in N(A)$ acts multiplicatively and identically on $A\otimes_F(I/I^2)$ by step 2. Substitution into those products proves identity action on $A\otimes_F(I^i/I^{i+1})$. For $i=0$ the quotient is $F$ with identity action by the jet lemma. Hence $h$ is identity on every successive quotient of $V=J^0\supseteq J^1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq J^{r+1}=0$.

source.place: Proposition 14.23, passage to powers of the maximal ideal and the displayed flag, printed p.285.

proof.text: Choose an $F$-basis of each $J^i/J^{i+1}$, lift it to $J^i$, and order these lifts with the deepest layer first. Together they form a basis of $V$. In this basis, $h_A(g)v-v$ lies in the span of earlier basis vectors for every basis vector $v$, every $F$-algebra $A$ and every $g\in N(A)$, by step 3. Therefore the representing matrix is upper triangular with diagonal entries $1$. Put $n=\dim_F V\geq1$ (the residue quotient is $F$). This gives a homomorphism $h:N\to\mathcal U_{n,F}$ with the same kernel $Z(G)$ as in step 1; the matrix equations hold for arbitrary $A$, hence define the factor as a group-scheme homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 14.23, final flag argument; Theorem 14.5(a)⇒(b) and Corollary 14.6, printed pp.281--282,285.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $h:N\to\mathcal U_{n,F}$. Its hypotheses require finite-type separated group schemes over a field, with no smoothness or connectedness requirement on the source. They hold: first apply the kernel clause of that same node to $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$ to obtain that $N$ is closed and of finite type; being closed in the affine $G$ it is affine and separated. Also, $\mathcal U_{n,F}$ is affine with polynomial coordinate algebra $F[x_{ij}:i<j]$. We obtain a closed subgroup scheme $U\subseteq\mathcal U_{n,F}$ and $q:N\to U$ having the same scheme-theoretic kernel as $h$, namely $Z(G)$. The kernel clause of that node gives the required equality on every $A$-point, even when $A$ has nilpotents.

source.place: Theorem 5.39, printed p.108, applied to the representation constructed in Proposition 14.23; quotient interpretation in Theorem 5.28, printed p.105.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 14.23, printed p.285, expanded using Corollary 8.10 and the homomorphism theorem 5.39.

lean.note: N is specified by its exact closed represented adjoint-kernel subfunctor on every algebra, using dual-number conjugation. Closed U in the unitriangular group is equivalently a closed subgroup of GL_n satisfying the upper unitriangular equations on all algebras.
